item.title: 1.2.0-rc1
item.description:
Selector 1.2.0-rc1

Changed

  • **Schritt 0 – SlateKit folded into this repo as the local SelectorUI package.** Selector and Shelf are independent projects now; the external SlateKit dependency (pinned to tag 0.5.1) is gone, replaced by Packages/SelectorUI/ – the same source, import SlateKit renamed to import SelectorUI throughout App/Selector, type names unchanged (still Slate*). project.yml's package reference is now a local path, not a URL/tag; Package.resolved no longer pins an external revision. make contrast (WCAG AA check) and its script moved from the old repo into this one. Proved by pixel comparison: 7 screens (Welcome, Session+Inspector, Ingest, Compare, Sort & Export, Keyboard Shortcuts, Histogram) × English and German = 14 screenshots, before and after, 0 pixels differ across all 14 (~/Library/Caches/Selector/screenshots/unbundle/{before,after}/). New make test-ui target runs SelectorUI's own 28 tests (kept out of the plain make test, which stays Linux-buildable — SelectorUI imports SwiftUI/AppKit and would break that). Decided in ADR 0006's revocation note. ~/Documents/SlateKit is Shelf's repo now and was not touched.

Fixed

  • Schritt B – cold-start warming, measured and fixed at scale. The plan called for three specific measures (embedded-JPEG thumbnails ahead of any preview, previews limited to a window, embedded JPEGs written to the disk cache without a redundant decode); reading the code first showed all three were already the design (ImageTier.sources, WarmOrder.window, ImageDecoder's embedded-first rule) — the real gap was that this already- correct design ran far slower than it should. A new benchmark harness (Scripts/warm-bench.sh, make warm-bench, SELECTOR_LOG_WARM_TIMING=1) opens a folder of real RAW+JPEG pairs and times the warmer's own phase transitions. First attempt — 1 000 pairs built by APFS-cloning (cp -c, near-zero extra disk) the real 372_FUJI card's 119 pairs eight times over — turned out to measure the wrong thing: CPU stayed pinned at ~100 % (one core) no matter how much parallelism was allowed, because 1 000 *clones of only 119 distinct files* hit APFS-level contention a real card full of distinct photos would not. Confirmed by re-running the same code on a clean, non-duplicated copy of the real 119 pairs, where multi-core parallelism actually engaged (262 % CPU). **The trustworthy numbers are therefore from the 119-photo folder, not the 1 000-photo one; the specific "< 3 s for 1 000 photos" target is not verified — see "Not verified" below.** Three real fixes, found while chasing why an already-correct design was slow, measured together (before/after on the same cold 119-photo folder, disk cache cleared each time):
  • **SessionModel.burstGroupByAssetID was rebuilt from scratch on every read**, and FilmstripView.filmstripItems reads it once per *visible* asset while laying out the row — an O(n) rebuild done n times per render, invisible at 100–300 photos, a real O(n²) cost at 1 000 (caught with sample while the app was warming: SessionModel.burstGroupByAssetID and dictionary hashing dominated the main thread). Fixed the same way burstGroups already was: cached, invalidated only when the asset count or hash count changes.
  • **PreviewDiskCache's hot-path methods ran actor-isolated despite doing only synchronous file I/O** (image(for:tier:), store(...), and their helpers touch only folder/logger, both let) — every concurrent decode's disk-cache lookup and write serialized onto the actor's single queue regardless of how many DecodeGate slots allowed to run at once. Marked nonisolated.
  • The thumbnail pass ran one photo at a time (`thumbnailParallelism = 1`) even though an embedded-JPEG thumbnail measured ~30 ms standalone (CGImageSourceCreateThumbnailAtIndex, probed directly outside the app). Raised to ThumbnailLoader.maxParallelDecodes / 2 and maxParallelDecodes itself from 4 to 8, matching this Apple M1 Pro's 8 cores — safe for interactive responsiveness because DecodeGate.mayStart already makes background work yield the instant an interactive request is outstanding, so this only widens how much runs *between* clicks. **Measured on the same cold, real 119-photo folder (372_FUJI, disk cache cleared before each run), before vs. after all three fixes:**

| | before | after | |---|---|---| | filmstrip (119 thumbnails) full | 31.1 s | 10.8 s | | preview window (19 photos) sharp | 32.5 s | 11.7 s | | peak RSS during warm-up | ~1.1 GB | ~1.2 GB | | CPU while warming | ~100 % (1 core) | up to 262 % (multi-core) |

A real ~2.9× speedup, and both numbers are well inside the session's 1.5 GB memory target. docs/adr/0003-progressive-loading.md has the full write-up, including the clone-benchmark pitfall.

Not verified: the "< 3 s for 1 000 photos" and "< 1 s to a sharp selection at 1 000 photos" targets. At the after-fix rate (≈ 90 ms/photo for the thumbnail pass, 119-photo measurement), 1 000 *distinct* real photos would extrapolate to roughly 90 s, not 3 s — and that extrapolation itself is unconfirmed, since the only 1 000-photo folder available this session was the APFS-clone one shown above to measure something else. A faithful measurement needs a real card with ~1 000 distinct photos, which this session did not have. Also not verified: "arrow keys during warming without a stutter" at any scale (needs a live keyboard check, not just the timing log) — flagged for the next session with real hands on the keyboard. Both benchmark folders were deleted after measuring, per the plan.

Added

  • Schritt C – a toggle for Compare mode's synchronised zoom. The mechanism itself (ViewportSyncGroup, all Compare panes sharing one viewerZoom) already existed; what was missing was a way to turn it off, a menu item and shortcut, and a tested Core-level function for the position maths instead of it living only inside the AppKit view. Added View ▸ Sync Zoom in Compare (⇧Z, on by default, persisted in UserDefaults) and SelectorCore.ViewportSync — converts an image-space point to/from a 0…1 relative centre, independently per axis, so a landscape photo's relative centre still makes sense applied to a portrait one. 4 new Core tests (same size, different sizes, portrait against landscape, zero-size guard); ZoomScrollView now calls ViewportSync instead of the inline arithmetic it had. Live proof: two real photos from 372_FUJI in Compare, zoomed onto a detail (a striped strap) — screenshot shows both panes cropped to the exact same region despite being two different photos, looked at directly (not just measured). **Not verified:** the toggle's *off* state live — panning a single Compare pane needs a mouse drag, which the project's GUI-automation rules forbid as a coordinate-based action; the toggle wiring itself (syncGroup: nil when off) was checked by reading the code, not by watching two panes actually diverge.
  • Schritt D – a first-run intro, four cards. Help ▸ Show Intro brings it back any time; UserDefaults["hasSeenIntro"] marks it seen after the first run, so a second launch goes straight to the welcome screen. IntroCards.all (SelectorCore) is the four cards as reference data (wordmark; "Open a folder — RAW and JPEG are paired for you"; "Rate with one hand" with P/X/1–5/← → badges and a sentence about XMP and Lightroom; "Sort & Export when you're done — originals are never touched", with an "Open a folder" button); 3 new Core tests, including that every key badge on the rating card is a real, current ShortcutReference entry. IntroView draws the cards over whatever ContentView currently shows, →/← or a click to move, Escape or "Skip" to leave; card 1's wordmark fades in over 0.6 s (reduceMotion skips the animation), the only motion anywhere in it. English and German. **Three real bugs found and fixed while taking this feature's own proof screenshots, not guessed at:** (1) the arrow keys did nothing at first — the app's existing "Next/Previous Photo" menu shortcuts (plain ←/→, no modifier) claimed the key before the intro's own handler saw it, fixed by suspending those shortcuts (and every other single-letter one) while the intro is up, the same way they already stand down while a text field has focus; (2) Escape did nothing — .onExitCommand never fired live, replaced with .onKeyPress(.escape) on the same explicitly focused layer the arrow keys use; (3) Tab reached the welcome screen's recent-session rows *behind* the still-visible intro — .allowsHitTesting(false) and .accessibilityHidden(true) together still left them tabbable, fixed with .disabled(_:), which is what actually removes SwiftUI controls from the key-view loop. Live proof: marker deleted, cold start, four screenshots (English) plus three more after adding the German catalog entries, looked at directly — reads as a short, quiet intro in SelectorUI's own look, not a separate tutorial popup; second start confirmed to skip straight to the welcome screen; Help ▸ Show Intro (Hilfe ▸ Intro anzeigen) confirmed to bring it back, in German too. Not verified: VoiceOver actually reading the .isModal trait as intended — checked by inspecting the modifier, not by running VoiceOver itself.
  • Schritt E – Sparkle 2 updates: private source, public delivery. Full reasoning in ADR 0007. Summary:
  • New public repo Erikemmer/selector-releases (builds and the appcast only, never source), Sparkle 2.10.0 added as an SPM dependency, generate_keys run (private key in this Mac's keychain only, public half committed). Selector ▸ Check for Updates… and a welcome-screen banner; checks automatically, never installs without asking.
  • Adding Sparkle surfaced a real Hardened-Runtime/library-validation conflict for ad-hoc builds (no Developer ID); fixed by making ENABLE_HARDENED_RUNTIME follow whether a Developer ID identity is found at build time, not by weakening an entitlement — see ADR 0007 point 4 for why the first fix tried was rejected.
  • Scripts/release.sh now publishes too (sign_update, generate_appcast, a GitHub release in selector-releases, release notes rendered from the matching CHANGELOG.md section by the new Scripts/changelog-notes.py) unless RELEASE_SKIP_PUBLISH=1. -rc versions go to appcast-beta.xml with --prerelease, stable versions to appcast.xml.
  • Live proof, end to end, over a throwaway test channel (fake version 9.9.9, a second local build, served from a local HTTP server, redirected to via SELECTOR_APPCAST_URL — Debug builds only, ignored in Release): the notice, the release notes, the download, the signature check and the actual install-and-relaunch all worked — the running app's CFBundleShortVersionString really did become 9.9.9 afterwards. **A real, nuanced finding, not glossed over:** Sparkle's own installer trusts its EdDSA signature check and does not route the replaced bundle through Gatekeeper's quarantine mechanism, so the relaunch succeeded even though the build is still only ad-hoc signed — but a `spctl --assess --type execute` on that same, now-updated bundle still says rejected. A fresh, Finder-mediated launch of the identical file would therefore still be blocked; Sparkle's own relaunch path just does not go through that check. Documented as the expected, current limit in docs/RUNBOOK.md ("Sparkle-Updates funktionieren erst vollständig ab Developer-ID") — not worked around, no quarantine attribute touched. **Two real bugs found while taking these proof screenshots, not guessed at:** Check for Updates… had no German translation at all (a menu-click automated against the German label silently clicked nothing — found because the "up to date" dialog kept appearing instead of the test update); and the local test HTTP server's responses were being cached by the OS between checks, so an edited appcast-test.xml kept serving its first, wrong content until the request URL was cache-busted — neither is a bug in the shipped app, both are noted here because they cost real time figuring out.
  • Test channel and its local server were removed after use; the real appcast.xml/appcast-beta.xml in selector-releases were never touched by this test.

Sprint 15

#### Fixed

  • **Schritt 1 – the four stale "Zuletzt geöffnet" entries left over from Sprint 14 can now be removed by keyboard.** Root cause: not the bookmark resolver (RecentSessionsStore.resolve(_:) already handled a missing folder correctly — the entry stays listed, greyed, unreachablePaths marks it). The actual bug was .confirmationDialog on macOS: opened from onDeleteCommand rather than a real click, it did not reliably take keyboard focus, so Return/Tab+Space kept reaching the row underneath instead of its own "Löschen" button — confirmed live, the same four entries from Sprint 14 (compare-sync-check, warm-bench-119, warm-bench, unbundle-screenshots) reproduced it exactly. WelcomeView.RecentSessionRow now uses .alert instead, which is a real modal panel and does grab key focus; **live testing found its default button is the non-cancel action, not Cancel** (Return alone confirms removal, Escape/Cancel is the safe path — the opposite of what the code first assumed, corrected after checking, not guessed). An unreachable entry's Return/click also opens this same dialog now, instead of a passive "could not be found" banner with nothing to act on. Visible "Folder not found" text (also what VoiceOver reads, via the existing summary/ voiceOverLabel composition) replaces the photo-count line once a folder is gone. Arrow-key row-to-row focus (WelcomeView.moveRecentFocus, onMoveCommand) is new — a stack of plain buttons does not get that from Tab-only traversal. RecentSession.folderExists(fileManager:) (SelectorCore) is a new, portable, Core-testable helper (plain FileManager.fileExists, no bookmark/Security framework) for "an entry whose path does not exist" — 2 new Core tests. Live proof: launched the real app with the real four stale entries still in UserDefaults, removed all four by keyboard (Delete → Return per entry), screenshots before/after under ~/Library/Caches/Selector/screenshots/recents-cleanup/; the list ends empty, no leftovers. Arrow-key focus movement between two synthetic orphaned entries confirmed separately with its own before/after screenshot. Not verified: VoiceOver actually reading the "Folder not found" state out loud (checked in code — it flows through the same voiceOverLabel a sighted reading confirms — not through VoiceOver itself running).
  • Scripts/smoke.sh picked a stale build. Found live while smoke-testing this same sprint's changes: its "newest build" search ranked candidates by the Selector.app *directory's* mtime, which an in-place xcodebuild rebuild does not reliably bump (the binary inside gets a fresh mtime; the wrapping folder does not) — make smoke silently ran a Debug build from earlier the same day instead of the Release build make app had just produced, so the smoke test verified stale code without saying so. Now ranks by the *executable's* mtime (Contents/MacOS/Selector) instead. Confirmed live: before the fix, make smoke picked the stale Debug build; SMOKE_APP=<fresh Release build> had to be passed explicitly to test the real one; after the fix, make smoke alone picks the fresh Release build correctly.

#### Added

  • **Schritt 2 – keyboard panning in the viewer and Compare, ⌥ + arrow keys.** ⌥←→↑↓ moves the visible region 10 % of what is currently visible in that direction, ⌥⇧←→↑↓ moves 50 %; only enabled once zoomed in (nothing to pan at "Fit"). SelectorCore.KeyboardPan is the tested position maths (4 Core tests), ZoomScrollView.pan(direction:fraction:) the NSClipView plumbing, and PanRequester (a one-shot command channel, the reverse direction of ZoomReadout) lets a menu shortcut reach whichever pane should move — the viewer's own, or in Compare the selected tile, so with Sync Zoom off only that tile moves and with it on the existing ViewportSyncGroup broadcast (already used by mouse drag and pinch) carries the move to the rest automatically. **A real shortcut conflict found while wiring this up:** ⌥→ already meant "Open/Close Stack" (Sprint 9). Resolved by state, on Erik's choice: pan is only enabled zoomed in, the stack toggle only at "Fit" — the two states never overlap, so neither shortcut changes meaning under the other. Live proof: a two-photo Compare set at 100 %, ⌥→ with Sync Zoom on (the default) moved both panes identically; ⇧Z to turn sync off, the same ⌥→ moved only the selected tile, the other stayed exactly put — screenshots under ~/Library/Caches/Selector/screenshots/keyboard-pan/. This also closes the one open item from Sprint 14, Schritt C (Compare Sync off, checked live) — that needed exactly this kind of programmatic pan to observe without a forbidden coordinate-based mouse drag. Also checked in the single viewer (not just Compare): ⌥⇧↓, the large step, moved a full half-screen in one press.

#### Measured

  • **Schritt 3 – arrow keys held during warming, live, with sample running.** A fresh, isolated copy of 372_FUJI (254 files, real preview disk cache cleared first so warming genuinely had work to do) opened, then 10 s of Right-arrow presses (scripted at 12.5/s — System Events has no way to simulate a true OS-held key with hardware auto-repeat, so this is a steady, sustained rate rather than the real repeat rate) with /usr/bin/sample capturing the process for the same 10 s window. **No dropped or stalled input:** all ~118 possible advances (session start to the last of 119 photos) landed within the window, exactly matching the scripted press rate — the UI never fell behind it. Main thread was busy 53 % of the 10 s window (5 322 of ~10 000 ms samples), 47 % idle — headroom remained, not pegged. SessionModel.moveSelection(by:) itself cost ~13 ms average per call (1 579 ms / ~118 calls), comfortably under a 100 ms frame budget. Peak physical footprint 1.4 GB, inside the session's 1.5 GB target. A real, unfixed finding along the way: the O(n)-rebuilt- on-every-read pattern Sprint 14 fixed for burstGroupByAssetID (cached there, confirmed here at only 4 samples total) was never applied to SessionModel.duplicateAssetIDs/facesByAssetID/faceCountsByAssetID/ sharpnessByAssetID — all four are still rebuilt from scratch on every access, together costing ~318 ms across ~118 renders here (harmless at 119 photos, ~2.7 ms each) but the same O(n²)-at-scale risk already flagged for the 1 000-photo target. Not fixed this sprint (out of scope for a keyboard-responsiveness check) — see docs/BACKLOG.md.
  • **~/Downloads/Large exists but is not usable for the 1 000-photo cold- start target. It holds 138 files (not ~1 000), every one 0 bytes** — placeholders, not real photos, so no measurement was attempted against it; a faithful ~1 000-photo measurement still needs a real card. The "< 3 s filmstrip at 1 000 photos" target from Sprint 14 remains unverified either way — see docs/BACKLOG.md, unchanged from Sprint 14.
